questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I went on the exchange to develop and challenge myself. I wanted to try to experience living and doing my studies in another country, meet new people, and be independent. Also, I went to improve my english skills.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a country that I felt safe living in and which had a nice international environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Choosing Amsterdam as my destination was the best choice I could make. The environment here is very international and open-minded.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You get a lot of valuable information before arriving and for the different procedures you have to keep in mind upon arrival. However, I had to write the administration at my home university and the University of Amsterdam a lot to get some further information or help for different procedures.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of e-mails with information about my staying. There was also an introduction meeting at the university where they informed about different things and what to expect from the university, grades and study load.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Every time I wrote the contact persons at the university they were good to answer and guide me through my problems. Also, the service at the university is nice and helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There was a procedure to apply for the off-campus accomodation. The procedure was pretty easy - so if you follow the steps and deadlines then this is a good opportunity to get student houseing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The accommodation I got through the university was the best I did. I lived in a dorm where about 200 people all were exchange students from different educations - so it was an easy way to meet new people. 
However, the dorm was about 30 minutes away from the city center - but if you have no problem with public transport or biking then it's fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In our dorm we had a common room and a rooftop where we could eat dinner together, have parties, and study. I got almost all my friends here and we were like a big family. Also, we were always a big group walking home from the city together when going out, because we were so many exchange students here - which made it feel very safe to go out. 
If you get the opportunity to choose the dorm "Fraijlemaborg", you should do it. 
It is a little away from the city - but the social network you get here is worth it. A lot of the other dorms do not have common rooms where you can meet up with the people - so a lot of people were jealous of our dorm.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course registration took some time and was a bit confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was a bit confusing knowing which courses I could take on the third block. But everything else regarding the courses was fine. 
However, you had a limited number of days to register which was a little stressful because I still had questions about some courses. But in the end the coordinators were very nice and helpful to help register and solve the problems I had with the registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write the coordinators and contact persons for help. They were very kind and helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I found out last minute that there was a course I was not able to take when trying to register. 
But otherwise, I got all the classes that I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be in good time about picking the courses you want and have some plan B courses in case you are missing some requirements. 
Also, don't be afraid to ask the coordinators for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level on the courses varies a bit. Some were harder than others. In total I would say that the level is compatible to the level of University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures and tutorials is kind of the same. However, there was in some courses weekly assignments sometimes with short deadlines which is part of your final grade. The structure of the semester is also different because it is divided into three blocks such that you have a course in 8 weeks. - That is something you have to get a little use to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Development, 
Development Economics, 
Public Finance and Fiscal Policy,
Natural Resource Economics, 
Industrial Organisation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Human Development was an interesting course. It was structured differently than the other courses but very informative.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: At the student housing, you maybe have to pay a municipality tax - that was unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transport was more expensive than expected. Some cultural things were a little expensive as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use any of these.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different classes you could take. It could be sports, creative courses or something else.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not use it, so I don't know. But some of my friends took Zumba classes and they really liked it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot to do in Amsterdam. Go see the cities which are close by fx Utrecht, Leiden, Den Haag, Zandvoort beach. Visit all the different museums and buy the museumkaart to safe a lot of money. Go to the parks in the city. And if you are here in the spring, then see some tulip fields.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite similar to Denmark - so it was easy. Also people in Amsterdam are very open-minded and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to talk to people in your classes. Everybody is very friendly and open-minded and that was how I got local friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very multicultural, which I really liked.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go to the Erasmus introduction week and all the activities in the beginning - You will get a lot of new contacts and friends there. 
- Don't invite too many visitors and enjoy your time here with the people you meet. 
- Remember to enjoy the time here and don't waste the time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a list with all the things you have to do both before and after arrival. You get a lot of information mails and you can easily forget something.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new people I met along the way and all the experiences I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To step out of my comfort zone and just talk to random people in different scenarios. - In the end it only paid off

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you go to Amsterdam you will not regret it. Best international environment and so many activities for students.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
